name: Kosaraju's Algorithm (SCC)
description: Finds all Strongly Connected Components using two DFS passes. Pass 1: DFS on original graph to record finish order. Pass 2: DFS on reversed graph in reverse finish order — each DFS tree is one SCC.
aim: Find all Strongly Connected Components (SCCs) in a directed graph — groups of nodes where every node can reach every other node. Uses two DFS passes: one on the original graph and one on the reversed graph.
howItWorks: Run DFS on original graph; push each finished node onto a stack
Reverse all edges in the graph
Pop nodes from stack; run DFS on reversed graph from each unvisited node
Each DFS tree in pass 2 is one Strongly Connected Component

time.worstCase: Always two DFS passes, no priority queue

realWorld: Social network analysis: find communities where everyone follows everyone else
Compiler optimization: detect loops in control flow graphs
Web ranking: Google uses SCC analysis to understand link structure
whenToUse: Finding groups of mutually reachable nodes in directed graphs
Simplifying graphs by condensing SCCs into single nodes
alternatives: Tarjan's Algorithm: single DFS pass O(V+E), same complexity
